front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The nucleus is composed of protons and neutrons.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
The nucleus is composed of positively charged **protons** and neutrally charged **neutrons**, so it has an overall **positive** charge.

front_blocks.md: Define **proton number**.

back_blocks.md: The **proton number**, or atomic number (*Z*), is the number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom.

front_blocks.md: What does the **nucleon number** represent?

back_blocks.md: The **nucleon number**, or mass number (*A*), represents the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus of an atom.

front_blocks.md: Define **isotope**.

back_blocks.md: **Isotopes** are atoms of the same element that have the **same** number of **protons** but a **different** number of **neutrons**.

An element may have only one isotope.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
An element may have more than one isotope, and some isotopes are **radioactive**.

front_blocks.md: The nuclide notation for an isotope of iron is `Fe presubscript 26 presuperscript 58`. How many neutrons does an atom of iron `Fe presubscript 26 presuperscript 58` contain?

back_blocks.md: An atom of iron `Fe presubscript 26 presuperscript 58` contains **32** neutrons.
The number of neutrons = nucleon number − proton number = 58 − 26 = **32**.

front_blocks.md: Define **nuclear fission**. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: Nuclear **fission** is the **splitting** of a large, unstable **nucleus** into two smaller nuclei.

cards.front_md: Define **nuclear fission**. **(Extended Tier Only)**

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Neutrons and gamma radiation can be released in nuclear fission reactions. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **True.**
When a nucleus splits, the two smaller (daughter) nuclei are released along with **two or three neutrons**, and **gamma rays** are also emitted.
